title: What Happens When You Get Hangry?
sources: Anglia Ruskin University, 'Hunger really can make us feel hangry' (2022-07-06), Swami, Hochstöger, Kargl & Stieger, 'Hangry in the field', PLOS ONE 2022, doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0269629 (64 adults in central Europe, 21 days, five smartphone prompts a day; hunger associated with 37% of the variance in irritability, 34% in anger, 38% in pleasure; controlled for age, sex, BMI, dietary behaviour and personality; 'variance explained', not proof of cause; supports line 2 'tracked thirty-seven percent of grumpiness' (grumpiness = irritability, shortened for voice)): https://aru.ac.uk/news/hunger-really-can-make-us-feel-hangry-study

Cleveland Clinic, 'Is Being Hangry Really a Thing or Just an Excuse?' ('When you haven't eaten for a while, the level of sugar (glucose) in your blood decreases'; when it 'gets too low, it triggers a cascade of hormones, including cortisol (a stress hormone) and adrenaline'; 'low blood sugar may interfere with higher brain functions, such as those that help us control impulses'; supports lines 3-4): https://health.clevelandclinic.org/is-being-hangry-really-a-thing-or-just-an-excuse/

MacCormack & Lindquist, 'Feeling hangry? When hunger is conceptualized as emotion', Emotion 2018, doi 10.1037/emo0000422, via Neuroscience News / UNC ('hunger alone isn't enough'; 400+ US adults online: hungrier people rated ambiguous Chinese pictographs as more negative only after a negative image, neutral or positive images had no effect = the guess answer 'only bad moments'; lab study, 200+ students, rigged computer crash: hungry participants who reflected on their emotions did not show the rise in stress and hostility = line 9): https://neurosciencenews.com/hunger-angry-hangry-9308/

The Conversation, Jennifer MacCormack, 'When does hungry become hangry?' (2018-06-11; author's own summary of the same studies: hunger matters mainly in negative situations; hungry people who focused on their feelings were not hangry): https://theconversation.com/when-does-hungry-become-hangry-98065

NHS, 'Low blood sugar (hypoglycaemia)' (symptoms include hunger, anxiety or irritability, sweating, shaking, confusion; usually affects people with diabetes; see a GP if you don't have diabetes but get shaking, sweating, a fast heartbeat or confusion; used in the description, not voiced): https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/low-blood-sugar-hypoglycaemia/

Tease (next video): Ohio State Wexner Medical Center, 'Why do paper cuts hurt so much?' (2025-05-09; 'Our face, hands and fingertips are richly innervated', so a cut there hits more pain receptors; paper cuts usually heal in two to three days): https://health.osu.edu/health/general-health/why-do-papercuts-hurt

lines.text: What happens when you get hangry?
One study: hunger tracked thirty-seven percent of grumpiness. Does it sour everything, or only bad moments?
lines.caps: ONE *STUDY | *HUNGER TRACKED | *THIRTY-SEVEN | *PERCENT | OF *GRUMPINESS | DOES IT *SOUR | *EVERYTHING | OR ONLY *BAD | *MOMENTS?

lines.text: Skip a meal, and blood sugar dips,
so stress hormones surge, and impulse control slips.
Ever snapped, then realized you skipped lunch?
But here's the twist: hunger alone isn't enough.
Hungry people rated symbols after nasty or neutral photos.
Answer: only bad moments, after nasty photos.
People who noticed their feelings didn't get hangry.
Next Body File: paper cuts, and screaming fingertips. Still hungry?
